# Mandara Shell

> Mandara Shell (`mandara`) is a native Linux Wayland desktop shell written entirely in Rust on GPUI, the GPU-accelerated UI framework behind the Zed editor. It gives MangoWM, Niri, Hyprland and Umbriel a status bar, dynamic island, dock, launcher, sidebar, notification center, on-screen displays, wallpaper engine, desktop widgets, lock screen, login manager and a live settings app (Mandara Studio), all in one binary that uses under 100 MiB of RAM. It is free software under GPL-3.0-or-later.

Key facts:

- Repository: https://github.com/theHamdiz/mandara (author: Ahmad Hamdi, `theHamdiz`).
- Compositors: MangoWM (tags), Niri (scrollable tiling), Hyprland and Umbriel, all first-class. Mandara never edits the user's own compositor config. It writes drop-in files to `~/.config/mandara/generated/` and adds one include line.
- Install: one command that downloads the signed release and runs `mandara install` (Arch, Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora, openSUSE, Void, Alpine, Gentoo, Solus). Update from Studio → About → Update now.
- Configuration: `~/.config/mandara/config.toml`, watched live. Mandara Studio (`mandara studio`) edits the same file, with 31 pages of settings.
- Command line: almost everything the interface does is a documented command with JSON replies (`mandara msg <command>`, catalog via `mandara commands --json`), so scripts and AI agents can drive and inspect the desktop.
- Plugins: 73 first-party plugins are built in. Third-party plugins are written in Rust, compiled to a sandboxed WebAssembly component (`wasm32-wasip2`, WIT interface), hot-reloaded, and shared through a GitHub marketplace.
- Performance: under 100 MiB RAM, under 190 MiB video memory and about 0.1 % CPU when idle. Frames build in under a millisecond (0.1–0.2 ms measured), far inside the 6.94 ms budget of a 144 Hz display. Nothing animates or samples while it is off screen.
- Design: spring-physics animation, Material You (HCT) palettes from the wallpaper, OKLCH color blending, light and dark themes, 15 interface languages including right-to-left Arabic, Persian and Urdu.
